We’re seeing an elevated rate of 5xx responses and occasional request timeouts for the Orpheus-3B model impacting requests routed to the us-west cluster. Impact observed: some inference calls returning 5xx and a small percentage of flows timing out after 10s. From your side, this may show up as failed API responses or longer tail latencies for batch scoring jobs.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Autoscale triggered and additional instances are being brought up to increase capacity.

- SRE team is collecting request logs and trace samples; I’ve attached an initial log bundle for your reference.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Orpheus-3B: elevated 5xx/timeouts — preliminary findings

Quick update from the infra side:
- We correlate the spike with a kernel-selection optimization pushed in the 02:00 PDT deployment window. The optimization changed eviction thresholds for the KV cache on Orpheus-3B hosts which reduced effective cache headroom under bursty traffic.
- Under bursty request patterns (like parallel batch scoring) we saw eviction thrashing that increased latency and caused some downstream 5xx errors when request handlers hit starvation.
- Immediate mitigation: we reverted the kernel-selection flag and increased KV cache allocation by 20% on affected pools; we also increased instance count in us-west to absorb burst.
- Current status: error rate has fallen from a peak of ~4.2% to ~0.6% in the last 15 minutes and tail latencies are improving. Traces show fewer retry loops.

Next steps:
1) Full log/trace correlation and a deterministic repro to validate the hypothesis (SRE owning).
2) Postmortem draft with timeline and mitigation — I’ll attach a draft by 14:00 PDT.
3) Plan for a safer rollout of the kernel-selection change with canary gating.

I’ll join the 10:30 call to explain.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Orpheus-3B: elevated 5xx/timeouts — recovery update and RCA summary

Hi Laura — quick update following our investigation and mitigation.

Status: recovered — error rate returned to baseline (~0.1%) by 11:30 PDT and tail latencies are back to expected ranges. No further timeouts observed in the last 20 minutes.

Root cause (summary): a recent kernel-selection optimization unintentionally tightened KV cache eviction thresholds on Orpheus-3B hosts. Under bursty usage (notably parallel batch scoring), the cache began thrashing which amplified latency and caused a subset of request handlers to surface 5xx errors.

Mitigation taken:
- Reverted the optimization and increased cache headroom on affected hosts.
- Scaled up instance pool for us-west and applied temporary rate-smoothing on batch routes.
- Postmortem draft attached; we’ll schedule a follow-up on runbook updates and a safer rollout plan for the kernel-selection change.

Recommended customer actions:
- If you have critical batch runs, consider delaying non-urgent scoring for the next 24 hours while we complete validation.
- Share any traces you captured and we’ll correlate them directly (attach to the INC ticket).

Links:
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4721
- Postmortem draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cPostmortemLink

We appreciate your patience — we’ll share the finalized postmortem and a deployment schedule for the fix by EOD tomorrow.
